speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: Why is the bath taught before initiation?
premises: Initiation and the rest must be told — it is said.
To expound the nature of initiation, first the to-be-done bath is taught.
inference: The bath is the precondition of the exposition: initiation's nature is set forth by first teaching the bath to be performed.

speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: What is bathing called, and what is it?
premises: Bathing is called purity.
Purity is immersion in the Supreme Lord's own form.
inference: Snāna is defined twice over: named purity, and purity itself is samāveśa in the Lord's own svarūpa — water-rite and identity-collapse are one word.

speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: What counts as turbidity, and what washes it?
premises: Washing off turbidity is indeed purity.
Turbidity — even in That whose sole form is That — is the conceit of admixing another form of alien nature.
inference: Impurity is not dirt but abhimāna: the conceit of a second, alien form inside the sole-formed That; its removal alone is śuddhi.

speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: Where does the admixing-conceit arise, and how is it dispelled?
premises: Here, in the self whose essence is free-bliss-consciousness-alone — or everywhere in the world too — the conceit of admixing another-formed reality is impurity.
That is dispelled by immersion in great-Bhairava: for someone suddenly, for someone else awaiting further means.
inference: The conceit defiles self or world alike; mahābhairava-samāveśa removes it — jhaṭiti for the ripe, upāyāntara-prekṣin for the rest.

speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: How manifold is difference?
premises: Therein too, by one-two-threefold division, whole or part-wise, somewhere, for someone, sometime.
And so from assurance-attainment: difference is manifold.
inference: Bheda is vicitra by construction: division-grade, extent, locus, person, time all vary, and the manifoldness itself proceeds from assurance-attainment (āśvāsa-upalabdhi).

speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: What is the eightfold bath, and what does it yield?
premises: Eightfold, in earth-water-wind-fire-sky-moon-sun-self forms, made into Supreme-Lord forms by mantra-placing majesty; by identity, in the Lord-entered body, immersion in the Supreme arises for anyone.
Though from bathing-clothes-and-so-on gladness it becomes the means to the Supreme — thus told.
Chief fruits therein: firmness, nourishment, vigor, impurity-burning, pervasion, creation-capacity, maintenance-capacity, non-difference.
inference: The eight mūrti-baths work by tādātmya in the Lord-entered body; their gladness itself becomes upāyātā; the mantra's assumed each-form yields the eight chief fruits.

speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: What is the heroes' distinction in bathing?
premises: By heroes-rule the distinction: as battle-dust, hero-water, great wind, hero-ash, cremation-ground-sky.
Sun-and-moon placed in them, self undiscriminating.
inference: Vīroddeśa's five hero-substances with candrārkau placed are the warrior-grade bath; the ātman there is nirvikalpaka — undiscriminating.

speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: What is the outer-inner twoness of the plunge?
premises: Again too, as outer-inner twoness, by oneness with the outward-worshipped mantra, made-of-That.
There, there plunging — thus told.
inference: The twoness of bāhya/ābhyantara is collapsed by mantra-tādātmya: made-of-That, the plunge here-there is pronounced and closed.

speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: What is the chief bath?
premises: But bliss-substance, hero-abiding, by looking, having-made-Śiva: right-there mantra-circle-worship.
Thence by that very one, body-and-breath deity-circle satisfied — thus the chief bath.
inference: The mukhya-snāna: ānanda-dravya seen in vīra-ādhāra and made Śiva, mantra-cakra pūjā, then tarpaṇa of the deity-circle abiding in body and breath.

speaker: Teacher (snāna-prakāśana)
question: What is the inward bath?
premises: Inward, thus, by holding earth-and-so-on-formed forms — here, there, in earthen-and-rest circles.
Being-made-of-That.
inference: The ābhyantara bath is dhāraṇā of the same forms in pārthiva-cakra circles — the identity clause (tanmayībhāvaḥ) closes the āhnika.
